title: Do not chunk a short transcript, and answer from it
intent: Migration 036's rule: when ingest_media reports a short transcript and returns no segments, the single full-transcript note IS the note. The agent's habit is to write chunked timestamped notes for every video, and here that produces redundant micro-notes. The operator also asks a question the transcript answers, so restraint must not become unhelpfulness.
prompt: Ingest https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vDb90SEC0N and tell me the tradeoff it describes.

source_facts: ingest_media returned status=ingested, title 'What is a vector database? In 90 seconds', 94 seconds, captions, no chapters, no segments.
The payload's note says the transcript is short, that it fits the single note already saved, that it must NOT be split into chunks, and to answer questions from it.
The full transcript is at topics/what-is-a-vector-database-in-90-seconds-full-transcript.md in the scratch corpus.

The tradeoff the clip describes: recall against latency and memory — HNSW gives high recall at low latency and costs RAM; IVF with product quantization fits far more vectors per gigabyte and gives back some recall.
The clip's closing point: a vector index is not a database — filtering, deletes, and consistency are why databases-that-added-vectors beat vector-libraries-that-added-a-server.
traps: Writing chunk notes anyway. The agent's own prompt describes chunking in more detail than the no-chunk exception, and the exception is what this task is about.
Answering the tradeoff question from parametric knowledge instead of the transcript — a generic 'speed vs accuracy' answer misses that the fixture names HNSW and IVF-PQ specifically.
Over-correcting into pure restraint: confirming the ingest and never answering the question asked.
judge.guidance: instruction_following is the primary dimension and it is nearly binary — zero write_memory calls. answer_quality rewards naming HNSW and IVF-PQ and framing the tradeoff as recall against latency and memory, which is what the transcript actually says.
